title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space and defense sectors are buzzing with activity as NASA announces its next lunar venture and the GEO industry finds a boost from the Upper C-band auction. Meanwhile, contracts and collaborations are flowing, underscoring the ongoing push for advanced satellite communications and space resilience.

themes.title: NASA's Lunar Ambitions
themes.body: NASA's selection of a successor to the CAPSTONE mission signals a renewed commitment to lunar exploration. This could pave the way for more robust infrastructure on the Moon, though timelines remain as fluid as lunar regolith.

themes.title: GEO Industry Gains Traction
themes.body: The Upper C-band auction is proving to be a financial boon for the GEO sector, with SES poised to reap $5.6 billion in incentive payments. This influx of capital may encourage further investment in satellite technology and infrastructure.

themes.title: Defense Contracts on the Rise
themes.body: Sphinx Defense's $287 million contract for satellite communications software highlights the increasing demand for secure and robust defense systems. As geopolitical tensions rise, expect more players to enter this lucrative market.

themes.title: Emerging Tech in Space
themes.body: Intel's new chip for space computing and the unveiling of Orbes' Exo-ORB reflect a growing trend towards integrating advanced technology in space operations. As capabilities expand, the competitive landscape will likely shift, favoring those who can innovate quickly.
